newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada reports 2nd straight mthly budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Canada reports 2nd straight mthly budget surplus.

text.p: Canada's Finance Department said on Friday that Canada recorded its second straight monthly budget surplus in June, the first time that occurred since the late 1970s.
The budget surplus was C$1.503 billion in June compared with a C$653 million deficit a year earlier, the department said.
For May, the federal budget surplus was C$1.37 billion, compared to a deficit of C$582 million a year earlier.
As a result, the government's budgetary position improved by a net C$2.2 billion on a year-over-year basis, the department said.
For the fiscal year to date ending March 31, 1998, Canada's budget deficit was C$533 million, compared to a deficit of C$5.295 billion a year earlier, the Finance Department said.

During June, budgetary revenues were up 16.3 percent to C$1.8 billion, while program spending fell 0.9 percent to C$0.1 billion. Public debt charges were down C$0.3 billion or 6.6 percent, the department said.
The increase in revenues was due mainly to higher personal income tax and goods and services tax collections, as well as higher corporate income tax collections and employment insurance premiums.

The rise in personal income tax revenue was a one-time development, and the rise in employment insurance premiums was due to timing and would be reversed over the last half of the calendar year, the department said in its Fiscal Monitor publication.

The decline in program spending reflected the impact of previous budget actions, the department said. But the fall was partly offset by higher elderly benefit payments, increased subsidy transfers and costs related to the June federal election.
Budgetary transactions (in billions of dollars)
Program spending -7.93 -8.01 -23.22 -24.13
Operating balance +5.10 +3.19 +10.35 +6.15
Public debt charges -3.59 -3.84 -10.88 -11.44
Deficit/surplus +1.50 -0.65 -0.53 -5.30
Fin requirements (ex forex) -0.51 -2.35 -0.48 -6.66
Forex transactions -0.84 +1.45 +1.05 +0.45
(Note: Positive numbers indicate net source of funds. Negative numbers indicate net requirement for funds.)

The Finance Department said its financial requirements in June were signficantly lower, amounting to C$483 million in the first three months of the fiscal year compared to a net requirement of C$6.7 billion during the same period last year.
The department said there was a net repayment of unmatured debt of C$6 billion in the first three months of the 1997-98 fiscal year.
